artists.biography: Neon Neon is a collaborative project from producer Boom Bip and Gruff Rhys, the frontman for the Welsh rock band Super Furry Animals. They began work on the project in October 2006 originally under the moniker Delorean. In March 2008 the duo, by now calling themselves Neon Neon, released a full-length album entitled Stainless Style to generally positive reviews and earned a nomination for the 2008 Mercury Music Prize. Gruff Rhys cast doubt over the future of Neon Neon in a 2008 for the BBC: "I don't know about making another Neon Neon album because it was quite a specific record about [John] DeLorean's life story. If we did something in the future it would have to be something different. But it's nice that it did well and we get to play it live." Neon Neon remixed Oasis's song "To Be Where There's Life" from their Dig Out Your Soul album for inclusion as the B-side of Oasis's single, "I'm Outta Time." However, it was only released on the vinyl copy of the single. In December 2011, Neon Neon announced the release of a new song from their Stainless Style sessions. The song 'Wheels' is being released as part of the 'Complex' compilation, which celebrates the 10th anniversary of Lex Records. An NME article announcing the release of the song suggested that Neon Neon are to return to the studio in 2012 to record a second album. On January 8, 2013, the group posted a picture of Giangiacomo Feltrinelli to their official Instagram account with the subtitle "NN2", indicating that their second album will focus on him.

perplexity.description:
Stainless Style is the debut album by Neon Neon, a collaborative project between Gruff Rhys of Super Furry Animals and electronic producer Boom Bip, released in March 2008 on Lex Records. The album blends electronic, hip hop, and rock elements, creating a distinctive mid-1980s synth-pop sound that emerged somewhat unexpectedly during its production. Recorded between London and Los Angeles from 2006 to 2007, the album features a mix of catchy synth melodies, hip hop beats, and eclectic vocal styles, reflecting the duo’s intent to craft something entirely different from their previous work.

Within Neon Neon’s discography, Stainless Style stands as a unique concept album inspired by the life of John DeLorean, the automotive engineer and entrepreneur. It received positive critical attention for its inventive fusion of genres and clever storytelling, though commercially it reached a modest peak of number 67 on the UK Albums Chart. The album’s innovative approach and genre-blending style have made it a notable entry in the late 2000s electronic and alternative music scenes.
